title: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station double suicide bombing
description: Two suicide bombers attacked near Tel Aviv's old central bus station on January 5, 2003, killing 23 people, including eight foreign nationals, and injuring more than 100. The al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade claimed responsibility.

title: El Salvador Earthquake
description: An earthquake struck off El Salvador on 13 January 2001 at 17:33 UTC. USGS strong-motion documentation gives magnitude Mw 7.6. Official impact figures cited in a subsequent technical report were 944 deaths and 5,565 injuries, with more than 100,000 houses destroyed. Landslides caused extensive loss of life, including in Santa Tecla.

title: Gujarat (Bhuj) Earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Gujarat near Bhuj on 26 January 2001 at 03:16 UTC, India's Republic Day. USGS reports at least 20,000 fatalities, 166,836 injuries and nearly a million buildings damaged or destroyed.

title: Novye Aldi massacre
description: Russian OMON police conducted a house-to-house purge of the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, summarily executing at least 62 civilians. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled Russia responsible.

title: Second El Salvador Earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck the San Vicente region of El Salvador on 13 February 2001 at 14:22 UTC, one month after the January disaster. It killed 315 people and caused further destructive landslides and building collapses.

title: Daegu subway fire
description: An arson attack aboard a train at Jungangno station in Daegu spread to a second train on February 18, 2003. The fire killed 192 people and injured more than 140. Combustible interiors, smoke and failures in the evacuation response contributed to the disaster.

title: Iran Ilyushin Il-76 military plane crash
description: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Ilyushin Il-76 flying from Zahedan to Kerman struck Mount Sirach during its approach in poor weather on February 19, 2003. All 275 occupants died. The Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives describes a premature descent below the minimum descent altitude in poor visibility.

title: Kaduna religious riots
description: Christian-Muslim violence broke out in Kaduna on 21 February 2000 during a protest against proposed Sharia legislation. A state judicial commission reported at least 1,295 deaths in the February violence. Later violence in May is excluded from that count; people interviewed by Human Rights Watch believed the total across the 2000 riots was substantially higher.

title: The Station nightclub fire
location: West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States
description: Pyrotechnics ignited polyurethane foam during a concert at The Station nightclub in West Warwick late on February 20 local time, February 21 UTC. The rapidly spreading fire killed 100 people and injured more than 200.

title: Mozambique floods and Cyclone Eline
description: Cyclone Eline worsened severe flooding already affecting Mozambique in February 2000. The wider flood and cyclone emergency killed about 700 people and affected about two million; these are cumulative emergency totals, not deaths or displacement on the landfall date alone.

title: Bogoro massacre
location: Bogoro, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: FNI and FRPI fighters attacked Bogoro in Ituri on February 24, 2003, killing at least 200 civilians. The International Criminal Court convicted Germain Katanga in connection with the attack in 2014; Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui was acquitted in 2012.

title: SuperFerry 14 bombing
description: A bomb aboard SuperFerry 14 caused a fire near Manila Bay at about 00:50 on February 27, 2004, local time, February 26 UTC. The attack was attributed to Abu Sayyaf. The reported death toll of 116 includes missing passengers presumed dead.

title: Godhra train burning
description: A coach of the Sabarmati Express caught fire following an attack near Godhra station on 27 February 2002, killing 59 passengers, including Hindu pilgrims and activists returning from Ayodhya. The incident was followed by widespread anti-Muslim violence in Gujarat.

title: Madrid Train Bombings
description: Bombs exploded on Madrid commuter trains during the morning rush hour on March 11, 2004. Spanish government accounts distinguish 192 victims of the train attacks from a police officer killed in the related Leganes explosion on April 3. More than 1,800 people were injured in the train bombings.

title: Chattisinghpora massacre
location: Chattisinghpora, Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir, India
description: Gunmen rounded up Sikh residents in Chattisinghpora in Anantnag district on March 20, 2000 and shot them, killing 35 people.

title: US-led invasion of Iraq
description: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on March 20, 2003, and Baghdad fell on April 9. Iraq Body Count's 2005 dossier recorded 7,299 civilian deaths during the invasion period through April 30. This is a documented period total, not deaths on the opening day or a comprehensive estimate of all war mortality.

title: Nahrin earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck the Nahrin area of Baghlan Province on 25 March 2002. Later IFRC operational reporting estimated 800 deaths and 10,000 people left homeless. Early casualty estimates were substantially higher; this figure follows the later IFRC assessment.
sources: International Charter Space and Major Disasters

title: Park Hotel Passover massacre
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the Park Hotel in Netanya during a Passover meal on 27 March 2002, killing 30 civilians and injuring more than 100. The attack was one of the triggers for Israel's Operation Defensive Shield.

title: First Battle of Fallujah
description: US forces began an assault on Fallujah on the night of April 4, 2004, after four American contractors were killed. Iraq Body Count cites about 800 reported Iraqi deaths across the April siege and estimates that 572-616 were civilians. These cumulative figures are estimates, not a single-day count.

title: Air China Flight 129 crash
description: Air China Flight 129, a Boeing 767 flying from Beijing to Busan, struck Mount Dotdae during a circling approach to Gimhae Airport on 15 April 2002. Of 166 people aboard, 129 died and 37 survived.

title: Ryongchon train explosion
description: An ammonium-nitrate explosion at Ryongchon railway station on April 22, 2004, devastated the surrounding town. IFRC reported 161 deaths and about 1,300 injuries. The French government's accident archive records 76 children among those killed.

title: Bojaya massacre
description: On 2 May 2002, during fighting between FARC guerrillas and paramilitaries in Bellavista, Bojaya, a cylinder bomb launched by FARC struck the church where civilians had taken shelter. Colombia's victims authority later recorded at least 79 deaths and more than 100 injuries; earlier reports had put the toll at 119.

title: Enschede fireworks disaster
description: A fire at a fireworks depot escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people including four firefighters. The blasts destroyed around 400 homes.

title: Casablanca bombings
description: Coordinated suicide bombings struck several sites in Casablanca on May 16, 2003, including a Spanish restaurant and Jewish-associated targets. The reported total of 45 deaths includes 33 victims and 12 bombers; about 100 people were injured.

title: China Airlines Flight 611 disaster
description: China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747 traveling from Taipei to Hong Kong, broke up in mid-air about 20 minutes after takeoff and crashed into the Taiwan Strait. All 225 passengers and crew were killed.

title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked outside the Dolphinarium discotheque in Tel Aviv on June 1, 2001, killing 21 other people, most of them teenagers, and injuring at least 120.

title: Nepalese Royal Palace Massacre
description: A shooting at Narayanhity Royal Palace in Kathmandu on 1 June 2001 ultimately left ten members of Nepal's royal family dead, including King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and Crown Prince Dipendra. An official inquiry attributed the killings of nine relatives to Dipendra, who died on 4 June. Gyanendra succeeded him as king.

title: Jerusalem bus 32A bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked Egged bus 32A near Patt Junction in Jerusalem during the morning rush hour on 18 June 2002, killing 19 other people and wounding more than 70.

title: Bou'in-Zahra earthquake
description: An earthquake struck the Avaj and Changureh area of northwestern Iran on June 22, 2002 at 02:58 UTC, severely damaging villages in Qazvin and neighboring regions. A disaster-science field report recorded about 261 deaths.
sources: Japan Society for Natural Disaster Science

title: Uberlingen mid-air collision
description: A Bashkirian Airlines Tupolev Tu-154 carrying 69 people, including many children en route to a Spanish holiday, collided with a DHL cargo Boeing 757 over southern Germany. All 71 people on both aircraft died.
sources: German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation

title: Typhoon Utor (Feria)
description: Utor, known as Feria in the Philippines, passed northern Luzon on 4 July 2001 and caused destructive flooding and landslides. A subsequent monthly storm summary reported at least 168 deaths in the Philippines. The storm then struck southern China, where additional deaths occurred; those are not included in this Philippine toll.

title: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crash
description: Sudan Airways Flight 139, a Boeing 737, crashed near Port Sudan on July 8, 2003, killing 116 of its 117 occupants. After an engine failed following takeoff, the crew returned toward the airport; the aircraft struck terrain on approach in limited visibility.

title: Sknyliv air show disaster
description: A Ukrainian Air Force Su-27 crashed into spectators during an aerobatic display at Sknyliv airfield near Lviv on 27 July 2002. The disaster killed 77 people, including 28 children, and injured hundreds.

title: Sbarro Pizzeria Bombing
description: A suicide bombing at the Sbarro pizzeria in Jerusalem on 9 August 2001 killed 15 civilians initially and wounded about 130. Chana Nachenberg died in May 2023 after remaining unconscious since the attack, bringing the victim toll to 16, excluding the bomber.

title: Canal Hotel (UN Baghdad headquarters) bombing
description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Canal Hotel, the UN headquarters in Baghdad, on August 19, 2003. It killed 22 people, including UN special representative Sergio Vieira de Mello and other UN staff.

title: Russian passenger plane bombings
description: Two passenger aircraft departing Moscow were destroyed by suicide bombings over Tula and Rostov oblasts on August 24, 2004. Russia's report to ICAO counted all 90 occupants, including the attackers, as killed. Investigators identified explosive devices detonated in flight.

title: Beslan school siege
description: Militants seized School Number One in Beslan on September 1, 2004, holding more than 1,100 people hostage. Explosions and an armed assault ended the siege on September 3. The civilian death toll was 334, including 186 children; attackers also died.
sources: European Court of Human Rights case-law note

title: September 11 Attacks
location: New York City, Arlington, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, United States
description: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew commercial airliners into the World Trade Center towers and the Pentagon. A fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. 2,977 people were killed.

title: Jakarta Stock Exchange bombing
description: A car bomb exploded in the underground car park of the Jakarta Stock Exchange on 13 September 2000, killing 15 people. Four men were subsequently convicted in connection with the attack, including two soldiers sentenced to life imprisonment in August 2001.

title: 2001 Anthrax Attacks
description: Anthrax-contaminated letters, including mail postmarked 18 September 2001, caused 22 infections and five deaths in the United States. CDC estimated that 32,000 people began preventive antibiotics. The FBI closed its investigation in 2010 after concluding Bruce Ivins was responsible. A National Research Council review found the scientific evidence linking the letter material to a particular laboratory flask less conclusive than the Justice Department had stated.

title: MV Le Joola capsizing
description: The overloaded Senegalese ferry Le Joola capsized off The Gambia late on 26 September 2002 while traveling from Ziguinchor to Dakar. The official toll was 1,863 dead or presumed dead, and 64 people survived.

title: Beltway sniper attacks
location: Washington metropolitan area, Maryland and Virginia, United States
description: John Allen Muhammad and Lee Boyd Malvo carried out shootings across the Washington metropolitan area in October 2002. Beginning on 2 October, the regional series killed ten people and critically injured three before the suspects were captured on 24 October.

title: US-Led Invasion of Afghanistan
description: The US-led air campaign in Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001. The Project on Defense Alternatives estimated that 1,000-1,300 civilians were killed directly by bombing between that date and 1 January 2002. The recorded figure is the lower end of that estimate for the campaign period, not a count for 7 October alone.

title: USS Cole bombing
description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers rammed an explosive-laden boat into the USS Cole as it refuelled. Seventeen American sailors were killed and 39 wounded.
sources: US Naval History and Heritage Command

title: Bali bombings
description: Three bombs exploded in Kuta and Denpasar on Bali, including a large car bomb outside the Sari Club nightclub, in an attack linked to Jemaah Islamiyah. The bombings killed 202 people, mostly foreign tourists, and injured more than 200.

title: Daping coal mine gas explosion
description: A gas explosion at the Daping coal mine near Xinmi in Henan Province on October 20, 2004, killed 148 miners.

title: Typhoon Tokage
description: Typhoon Tokage crossed Japan on October 20, 2004, bringing destructive rain, floods and landslides. Official records list 95 deaths and three missing. It was the tenth typhoon to make landfall in Japan that year.
sources: Japan Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism

title: Niigata Chuetsu earthquake
description: The October 23, 2004, Niigata Chuetsu earthquake and subsequent activity caused 68 deaths and 4,805 injuries. JMA gives magnitude 6.8 on its scale. Some 3,175 homes were destroyed and peak evacuation exceeded 100,000 people.

title: Podi Coal Mine Explosion
description: A gas explosion at the Podi coal mine in Jiaocheng County, Shanxi, on November 15, 2001 killed 33 people. A subsequent investigation found that ventilation failures allowed gas to accumulate and that the mine had resumed production without the required authorization.

title: Chenjiashan coal mine gas explosion
description: A gas explosion at Chenjiashan coal mine near Tongchuan, Shaanxi, killed 166 miners. It occurred at about 07:10 on November 28, 2004, local time, November 27 UTC. Fire and toxic gases hampered rescue and recovery.

title: Ben Yehuda Street Bombings
description: Two suicide bombers struck the Ben Yehuda pedestrian area in Jerusalem on 1 December 2001, followed by a car bomb. Eleven people were killed and more than 130 injured. Hamas claimed responsibility.

title: Haifa Bus 16 Bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked bus 16 in Haifa on 2 December 2001, killing 15 other people and wounding about 40. The attack followed the previous night's bombings in Jerusalem.

title: Indian Parliament Attack
description: Five gunmen attacked India's Parliament complex in New Delhi on 13 December 2001. Eight security personnel and a gardener were killed, and all five attackers were shot dead. Indian authorities attributed the attack to Pakistan-based militant groups.

title: Luoyang Dongdu commercial building fire
description: A fire caused by welding work spread through the Dongdu commercial building in Luoyang on 25 December 2000, killing 309 people. Smoke reached a crowded dance hall; investigators said the welders left without raising the alarm.
sources: French Ministry of Ecological Transition, ARIA

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
description: The December 26, 2004, earthquake off northern Sumatra generated a devastating Indian Ocean tsunami. NOAA and UNESCO's 2024 summary records 227,899 people killed or missing and presumed dead in 15 countries, with about 1.7 million displaced.

title: Grozny government headquarters bombing
description: Suicide attackers drove explosive-laden vehicles into the Chechen government headquarters in Grozny on 27 December 2002. The reported victim toll was 83, excluding the attackers.

title: Rizal Day bombings
description: Coordinated bombings struck five locations across Metro Manila on a national holiday, killing 22 people. The deadliest blast hit a crowded LRT train.
